entries.400a5a09b8f1630d: As its corporate vision, "Vision 2030", the company has set "the comfort of wood, from homes to a variety of spaces", and its management strategy consists of concentrating on business areas that make use of the advantages of wood, strengthening competitiveness across a value chain that extends to a wider range of spaces, and strengthening the management foundation in both financial and non-financial terms. The company states that it will work to strengthen competitiveness in the new-build detached house market, develop the rental housing and renovation markets, and expand the value chain for non-residential fields (public, commercial and accommodation facilities), and it also intends to expand its lineup of domestically produced softwood plywood and domestically sourced wood products and diversify raw material procurement.

entries.995e5c42a4c771b9: The company manufactures a wide range of wood-based materials in-house, from plywood to fiberboard such as MDF and hardboard and interior materials, and has the Shimizu Works, the Fujikawa Works and group production sites such as Ishinomaki Plywood Industry. Its strength lies in a structure in which the group handles everything from material manufacturing to construction within the group, through sales with installation by its subsidiary Nafix (material-and-construction sales) and the design and construction of exterior structures by Arimoto Kogyo. The company also offers original products and construction methods, including the interior material series "Kanael", the structural panel "HBW", and the wood-frame sound-insulation and fire-protection method "Sharon".

entries.c09e7f7aea5b7da2: Revenue from external customers by segment for the fiscal year ended November 2025 was ¥39,804 million for the Wood-Based Building Materials Business and ¥24,881 million for the Plywood Business. Revenue by region is omitted from disclosure because revenue from external customers in Japan exceeds 90% of consolidated revenue. The major customers are SMB Kenzai (45.9% of revenue) and Itochu Kenzai (12.0% of revenue). The company views new housing starts, an industry demand indicator, as likely to decline in the future, while the underlying need to improve living environments remains strong and renovation demand is considered firm.
